q: Are hourly grid emission factors available for India, and will Scope 2 need them?
title: Hourly grid emission factors in India
short: No official hourly grid factors exist for India. The CEA publishes one annual factor, currently 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, and the GHG Protocol accepts it. Hourly factors may matter later: the draft Scope 2 revision proposes hourly matching for market-based claims, but nothing is final.
audience: Indian companies buying renewable power; data teams

p: The CEA CO2 Baseline Database gives annual figures for the national grid: the weighted average, operating margin, build margin and combined margin. There are no official hourly, monthly or state factors. Grid-India publishes real-time generation by source, from which analysts build unofficial hourly estimates, but these are not a recognised reporting factor and methods differ.

sections.h: What the current Scope 2 rules require
p: The 2015 GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance asks for the most precise location-based factor available. In India that is the annual CEA weighted average. Market-based claims today match certificates to consumption over the reporting year, not hour by hour.

The GHG Protocol consulted on a revised Scope 2 standard from October 2025 to January 2026. The draft proposes hourly matching of clean power to consumption for market-based claims, with deliverability tests, and more granular location-based factors where they exist. It published a summary of the feedback in July 2026. The final text and start dates are not set, and smaller reporters may get simpler options.

ul: Keep reporting with the annual CEA factor and name the version.
Keep interval data where you have it: HT meters and time-of-day bills already record consumption by time block.
Ask solar PPA, captive or open access suppliers for hourly or 15-minute generation data, and write it into contracts.
Avoid long contracts that only promise annual certificate volumes without time data.

example.title: Worked example: annual vs hourly matching (illustrative)
lines: Factory use: 1,000 MWh a year, 40% of it at night
Solar PPA: 1,000 MWh a year, all generated in daylight
Annual matching: 1,000 of 1,000 MWh covered, market-based Scope 2 = 0 t
Hourly matching: at most the 600 MWh used in daylight is covered; 400 MWh uncovered
Uncovered: 400,000 kWh x 0.710 = 284,000 kg, 284 t CO2
example.note: In practice hourly coverage would be lower still on cloudy days and in low-sun months.

senseible: Senseible uses the annual CEA weighted average (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, database version 21.0) for location-based Scope 2, and shows market-based Scope 2 separately once you add instrument data. No official hourly Indian factors exist for it to apply, and it does not run hourly matching.
